lesson.title: Verb-Final Gym
lesson.subtitle: omdat, dat, als, wanneer, maar, hoewel

hook.title: Six Connectors, One Destination
hook.content: Omdat, dat, als, wanneer and hoewel all send the verb to the end. Maar is a coordinator and keeps the main-clause order. The connector tells you which machine to use.

pattern.title: Subordinators vs coordinators
pattern.content: Omdat/dat/als/wanneer/hoewel → verb final. Maar/en/of → main-clause order. Ik werk, maar ik ben moe; ik werk omdat ik geld nodig heb.
pattern.trap_note: Do not treat maar like omdat. Maar joins two main clauses; omdat creates a subordinate clause.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Verb-Final Gym):
exercises.target_answer: omdat, dat, als, wanneer, maar, hoewel
exercises.meaning: because, that (conjunction; relative), if, when, as, when, but, although
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Verb-Final Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “I come because you are here.”?
options: Ik kom omdat jij hier bent.
niet Ik kom omdat jij hier bent.
Ik kom omdat jij hier bent. (1)
exercises.target_answer: Ik kom omdat jij hier bent.
exercises.meaning: I come because you are here.
exercises.explanation: “Ik kom omdat jij hier bent.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Verb-Final Gym”.

exercises.idea: I think that it is good.
cues: It means: I think that it is good.
idea_parts: I think that it is good.
exercises.target_answer: Ik denk dat het goed is.
exercises.meaning: I think that it is good.
exercises.explanation: “Ik denk dat het goed is.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Subordinators vs coordinators.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not treat maar like omdat. Maar joins two main clauses; omdat creates a subordinate clause.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.german: Als het regent, blijf ik thuis.
exercises.natural: If it rains, I stay home.
options: If it rains, stay I home.
If it rains, I stay home.
not If it rains, stay I home.
exercises.target_answer: If it rains, stay I home.
exercises.meaning: If it rains, I stay home.
exercises.explanation: “Als het regent, blijf ik thuis.” is word-for-word “If it rains, stay I home.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Subordinators vs coordinators.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Ik werk, maar ik ben moe.
exercises.target_answer: Ik werk, maar ik ben moe.
exercises.meaning: I work, but I am tired.
cues: It means: I work, but I am tired.
exercises.explanation: “Ik werk, maar ik ben moe.” reuses only material taught in “Verb-Final Gym” — Subordinators vs coordinators.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Ik werk, maar ik ben moe.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Subordinators vs coordinators.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “Although it is cold, I go.”
twist.target_answer: Hoewel het koud is, ga ik.
twist.explanation: Hoewel is a subordinator: is goes to the end of its clause; ga keeps main-clause order.

summary.outcome: Choose a subordinator or a coordinator and order the verb accordingly.

use_example.german: Ik werk, maar ik ben moe.
use_example.english: I work, but I am tired.

summary.takeaway: Connectors come in two species: those that move the verb and those that do not.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Relative Clauses & Connectors.

omdat.context_phrase: Ik kom omdat ik tijd heb.
omdat.context_translation: I come because I have time.
omdat.etymology_derivation: A subordinating conjunction; the verb goes to the end.

dat.etymology_derivation: The neutral demonstrative and conjunction; also the het-relative pronoun.

als.context_phrase: Als het koud is, blijf ik thuis.
als.context_translation: If it is cold, I stay home.
als.etymology_derivation: English as and also are the same root; Dutch als covers if/when/as.

wanneer.etymology_derivation: A compound question word; English when is the short cousin.

maar.context_phrase: Ik werk, maar ik ben moe.
maar.context_translation: I work, but I am tired.
maar.etymology_derivation: A short high-frequency conjunction; the vowel is long.

hoewel.etymology_derivation: hoe + wel, literally 'how well'; a subordinating conjunction.
